diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not force DD/MM/YYYY on US-locale receipts, ISO-dated receipts, or non-receipt documents; do not override an unambiguous MM>12 row.

diagnoses.label: negative_signed_payment_line_misread_as_total

The sign must either (a) exclude the line from total candidacy, or (b) be preserved so the arithmetic cross-check rejects it.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Selecting the last numeric token on a Visa/Mastercard/Cash line as the total because its absolute value matches the two-decimal invariant and the line is not strictly a tier-keyword candidate but gets reached via fall-through or free-text last-number scan.

The predicted value 702.00 does not appear on the receipt image at all, suggesting an OCR-corrupted number was chosen or a split-line fallback walked onto a non-total line and parsed digits mangled by Tesseract. The receipt clearly offers 538.00 on an unambiguous 'Total RM Including GST' and 'Total Rounded' pair.

When corroboration exists for value V and the chosen value differs by more than rounding tolerance, back off to the corroborated V. This is the existing multi_variant_consensus_over_tier_priority anchor, but it needs an explicit same-variant corroboration rule for IKEA-style 'Total ... / Total Rounded / Visa' triples.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Within the already-selected tier, prefer the candidate whose numeric value is corroborated by another total-adjacent anchor in the same OCR variant (Total Rounded, Grand Total, Net Total, or the absolute value of a payment line). Reject candidates that have no corroboration when a corroborated alternative exists at the same tier. Do not override tier priority — only disambiguate within a tier.

diagnoses.label: payment_tender_line_leaks_into_split_line_fallback
diagnoses.general_pattern: When the chosen keyword line's own numeric token fails to parse (OCR corruption like `92:80`, `tS 92.80`, or a trailing stray char), the extractor falls through to the next non-empty line and picks a payment/tender amount (Cash / Cash Received / Visa / Mastercard / Change) that happens to sit immediately below the total line. This produces an amount that is numerically plausible but semantically wrong (payment ≠ total; it typically equals rounded tender like 20.00 or 100.00, or the signed card charge).
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating 'keyword line has digits but monetary regex fails' as equivalent to 'keyword line has no digits', and therefore activating the split-line fallback that reads the last number on the following line without re-checking payment/tender exclusions on that fallback line.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 078.jpg prediction amount='' with date correct (2017-02-02); receipt visibly shows 'Grand Total : 92.80', followed by 'Cash Received : 100.00' and 'Change : 7.20'. Trajectory window shows explicit agent trace: variant 0 captured 'a Total — 92:80' and 'GrandTota. = tS 92.80' (keyword with digits that fail two-decimal parse), and the m0168 think step records that the fallback then considered the following line. Field feedback marks 078 amount_correct=false. Same shape in 074 (predicted 702.00, feedback amount_correct=false) where IKEA receipt shows 'Total RM Including GST 6% 538.00 ... Visa -538.00', and 087 which the agent eventually got right via tender exclusion shows the same risk surface.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before taking the split-line fallback, verify (a) the keyword line truly contains zero digits (not merely zero *parseable* two-decimal tokens), and if it contained digits that failed parsing, back off to an earlier same-tier candidate or escalate to a different OCR variant rather than reading the following line; and (b) if a fallback line is used, re-apply both the exclusion keyword set and the payment/tender keyword set (CASH, CASH RECEIVED, CASH TENDERED, TENDERED, PAYMENT, PAID, RECEIVED, CHANGE, VISA, MASTERCARD, MASTER, CARD, CREDIT, DEBIT) to that fallback line.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In `receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation` step 4, distinguish 'keyword line is digit-free' from 'keyword line has digits that failed the two-decimal regex'. Only the digit-free case may consult the next line; the digit-corruption case must back off within the same tier (try other same-tier candidates, other OCR variants, or `ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck`) and never silently consume a payment/tender line as the total.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-style OCR tasks that declare a keyword-priority total extraction contract with explicit exclusion and tender keywords; does not generalize to free-form document OCR or to tasks where the 'next line' is itself the authoritative amount field by contract.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Non-receipt OCR, forms where the amount is defined to appear on a line below a label by schema, or any task without a declared payment/tender exclusion set.

diagnoses.label: ocr_corrupted_total_token_not_normalized_before_fallthrough
diagnoses.general_pattern: Tesseract substitutions on the total-amount token (`92.80` → `92:80`, `tS 92.80`, `GrandTota. = tS 92.80`, `88.1` for `88.17`) cause the two-decimal regex to miss a valid total that is in fact present on the keyword line, and the pipeline then either falls through to the wrong line or emits null. The confusable-digit normalization anchor exists but is not applied aggressively enough to total-anchored lines before declaring the tier empty.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Running the strict two-decimal regex once on the raw keyword line and, on failure, immediately moving on (to split-line fallback or next tier) without first attempting confusable-digit substitution restricted to the numeric span of a total-anchored line.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Agent trace on 078 variant 0 shows the line captured as `a Total — 92:80` (colon instead of period) and `GrandTota. = tS 92.80` (letters prefixing the digits). Both are keyword-anchored lines on which `(\d+\.\d{2})` fails because of `:` or because of leading letters bleeding into the token. The agent attempted a candidate-voting rerun (m0165) but still landed on an empty amount for 078.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: On a total-anchored line where the two-decimal regex fails, apply `ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck` substitutions to the numeric span (`:` → `.`, `O/o/Q` → `0`, `l/I/|` → `1`, `S` → `5`, `B` → `8`, `tS` prefix stripped, etc.) and re-apply the two-decimal regex to the same line *before* either falling through to the next line or declaring the tier empty.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Chain `monetary_two_decimal_invariant` → `ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck` on each candidate keyword line as a single composite extraction step; only treat the tier as empty when both the strict and the normalized regex fail on every candidate.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Apply confusable substitution only inside numeric spans on lines already matched by a total/amount tier keyword; do not apply to free text, product descriptions, IDs, phone numbers, or dates.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Free-text normalization, product-code parsing, or any task where letter→digit substitution would corrupt identifiers.

diagnoses.label: multi_variant_consensus_overweights_frequency_vs_corroboration
diagnoses.general_pattern: When multiple preprocessing variants yield different candidates for the total line, the pipeline selects by majority frequency across variants, which can lock in a wrong value if two of three variants degrade identically. The anchor already specifies corroborated_support (subtotal match, cash − change, payment match) should dominate over cross-variant frequency, but the implementation observed in the trajectory ranks cross-variant support higher than corroboration.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Ranking candidates by `(tier_rank, cross_variant_support, position)` and taking the modal value across variants without first checking whether a lower-frequency candidate is corroborated by a subtotal/tax/payment-change arithmetic anchor on the same receipt.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 074.jpg prediction 702.00 vs amount_correct=false; receipt shows '538.00' as Total RM Including GST and '-538.00' as Visa, and '2 pc @ 269.00 = 538.00' as the line-item. 702 does not appear anywhere on the receipt as a two-decimal total, suggesting a cross-variant OCR hallucination (e.g. `TD2.00` or `702.00` from a mangled region) won majority voting over a corroborated 538.00 that was discoverable via the subtotal/payment echo. Trajectory m0162/m0165 shows the agent explicitly swapped to candidate voting on this run.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before majority voting across OCR variants, run the arithmetic cross-check from `ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck`: if a candidate value is corroborated by a parsed subtotal + tax − discount (within rounding tolerance) or by a payment-tender line that equals it, that candidate outranks a numerically different modal candidate even if the modal candidate appears in more variants.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In `multi_variant_consensus_over_tier_priority` step 2, implement corroborated_support as a strict precedence over cross_variant_support, and treat cross_variant_support only as a tie-breaker among equally corroborated candidates at the same tier.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipt-style OCR where subtotal/tax/payment lines are frequently present; do not apply arithmetic cross-check when neither subtotal nor payment is parseable.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Free-form OCR tasks without an arithmetic invariant, or any task where the 'total' is not a sum of line items.

diagnoses.label: null_vs_empty_string_writeback_violated_on_extraction_failure

diagnoses.label: ocr_corrupted_total_line_triggers_tier_fall_through_or_bad_fallback_instead_of_stronger_variant
diagnoses.general_pattern: On receipts where the correct tier's keyword line is present but its own numeric span is OCR-corrupted (letters inside digits, missing decimal, concatenated '92:80' or '92-80', or the keyword itself is split like 'Grand Tota.'), the extractor either (a) accepts a corrupted number from the same line, (b) falls through to a lower tier that matches an unrelated 'Total' column header or a different summary line, or (c) emits null. The structurally correct fix is to re-run OCR on that line with stronger preprocessing (higher upscale, different PSM) and re-parse, rather than degrading tier or giving up.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: On receipt 078 (THAI DELICIOUS RESTAURANT), the ground-truth summary lines are 'Total : 92.80' and 'Grand Total : 92.80'. The source Agent's own OCR variants produced 'a Total — 92:80' and 'GrandTota. = tS 92.80'. The agent's regex requires '\bGRAND\s+TOTAL\b' (whitespace between words), so 'GrandTota.' never matches, and the ':' in '92:80' breaks the two-decimal regex. Instead of triggering the conditional multi-pass fallback with 3x upscale + PSM 4 (which the agent later verified does yield 'Grand Total a 92.80'), the agent emitted an empty string. Analogous OCR noise on 074 and 077 likely selected wrong candidates in-tier.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: field_feedback rows show amount_correct=false for 074.jpg (predicted '702.00'), 077.jpg (predicted '23.26'), and 078.jpg (predicted ''). The agent's own debug thought (message m0192) explicitly records: 'Upscale 3x with PSM 4 gives "Grand Total a 92.80"!', confirming the stronger-variant path recovers the correct line. For 077 (HON HWA HARDWARE), the predicted '23.26' matches a line unrelated to this receipt's own 'Total Inclusive GST: 10.40' / 'Total 10.40' structure, consistent with cross-contamination from a wrong candidate or a bad fallback. For 074 (IKEA Cheras), '702.00' does not match 'Total RM Including GST 6% 538.00' / 'Total Rounded 538.00', again indicating in-tier or fallback mis-selection rather than a tier-list defect.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: After the keyword-priority tier selects a candidate line, before accepting its numeric token or falling through, test the token against the two-decimal invariant and (where subtotal/tax are both reliably parsed) an arithmetic-plausibility window. If the token fails either test, invoke conditional_multi_pass_ocr_on_noisy_numeric_fields with at least a 3x upscale and PSM 4 variant and re-parse the same line. Only after that retry still fails may the extractor fall through to a lower tier or emit None.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Treat an OCR-corrupted total line as a signal to escalate OCR effort on that line, not as a signal to change tier. Compose receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation with monetary_two_decimal_invariant and conditional_multi_pass_ocr_on_noisy_numeric_fields: tier chooses which line, invariant decides whether the number is trustworthy, multi-pass fallback is triggered when the invariant fails, and only after a bounded set of variants fails do we degrade tier or abstain.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-style OCR tasks that declare keyword-priority total lists; strictly a post-tier-selection retry policy on the chosen line.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Non-receipt OCR, free-form document OCR, or any task without a declared tier-priority list for totals; do not use multi-pass escalation to override a clean higher-tier match that already passes the two-decimal invariant.

The predicted amount '702.00' does not appear in that summary block as a positive-sign total, so the writeback could not have come from a top-tier anchored match.

diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation strictly: build canonicalized lines, drop exclusion-keyword and tabular-header lines, then within the first non-empty tier accept the last line passing monetary_two_decimal_invariant on its own text. Do not fall through tiers when a higher tier has any surviving candidate.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-style OCR extraction tasks that declare a keyword priority list and exclusion list in their prompt.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Non-receipt OCR, generic text extraction, PDF table extraction, vision-model OCR of free-form documents.

diagnoses.label: amount_confusable_normalization_missed_on_077_shell
diagnoses.general_pattern: Petrol/fuel receipts frequently have the total line printed in a condensed/noisy font that causes Tesseract to substitute letters for digits inside the monetary token on a line that itself matches a declared total keyword (e.g. 'Total RM 86.00'). The two-decimal invariant must be applied after bounded confusable substitution restricted to tokens that are already digit-dominated and sit on a tier-matched line.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Either (a) accepting a confusable-corrupted token verbatim (yielding e.g. '23.26' when the keyword line actually reads '86.00' after normalization), or (b) applying confusable substitution to free text/IDs, or (c) refusing to normalize and falling through to a lower tier.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 077.jpg amount_correct=false, date_correct=true. The image shows a Shell fuel receipt with a 'Total RM 86.00' line and a '6.00% GST A RM 4.87' line among others; the predicted amount '23.26' is numerically unrelated to the fuel-total block, suggesting the extractor either took a value from an unrelated receipt region or picked a confusable-corrupted non-tier candidate.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: On the chosen tier-matched line, re-run the two-decimal regex after applying the confusables table (O/o/Q→0, l/I/|→1, S→5, B→8, Z→2, G→6, u→0) only inside digit-dominated tokens; if arithmetic cross-check with a reliably parsed subtotal+tax is available, prefer the arithmetically consistent candidate.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck guarded by the tier-match and the digit-dominated-token condition; never apply substitution to IDs, phone numbers, or dates.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only when the candidate token sits on a line that matched a declared total/amount tier keyword and is already digit-dominated.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Normalizing arbitrary numeric fields (quantities, invoice IDs, phone numbers, GST registration numbers, dates) or applying substitution on free-text lines.

diagnoses.label: empty_string_written_instead_of_null_on_078_mynews
diagnoses.general_pattern: When total extraction fails, the task contract requires the cell to be a true null; writing an empty string instead violates the null-vs-empty-string contract and will also typically indicate that a guarded split-line fallback was not attempted even when the task prompt declares one.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Returning '' from the extraction function on failure and assigning that empty string to the openpyxl cell, instead of returning Python None and letting openpyxl write a genuinely empty cell. Additionally, giving up before applying the guarded next-line fallback when the keyword line contains zero digits.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 078.jpg prediction row has total_amount='' (empty string) with amount_correct=false while date_correct=true. The predictions table shows every other row carries a two-decimal numeric string; this single-row empty string is a distinct writeback value and confirms the sentinel was not routed through None. The image (a myNEWS receipt) contains 'GRAND TOTAL' and 'SUB TOTAL' lines where the amount sits on the same or an adjacent line, so a guarded same-line or split-line read is in scope.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: On extraction failure, (1) attempt the guarded split-line fallback only when the keyword line has zero digits and the following line is pre-cutoff, non-exclusion, non-payment; (2) if still unresolved, return Python None (not ''), and assign None directly to the cell without any str()/f-string coercion.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Compose receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation (step 4 guarded split-line fallback) with null_vs_empty_string_contract on the writeback side, mirrored by xlsx_delivery_contract_self_check which asserts cell.value is None for failed cells.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt-extraction tasks whose contract declares that failed extractions must be null in the output cell.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Tasks whose contract uses '' as a sentinel, requires a specific placeholder string, or where the output format never distinguishes null from empty.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: null_vs_empty_string_contract (and cross-reference xlsx/SKILL.md 'Preserving null vs empty string on writeback')

diagnoses.label: non_transaction_date_selected_on_034_zheng_hui
diagnoses.general_pattern: Receipts frequently carry multiple date-shaped tokens (transaction date, print timestamp, closing date, promo date). Taking the first regex match or the lexically latest date without binding to a 'Date:' / 'Invoice Date' label (and excluding 'PRINT', 'CLOSED', 'CLOSING' prefixes) yields a non-transaction date.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Selecting the first date-shaped token in the OCR text or the date on a 'PRINT BY' / 'CLOSED' / 'FRN ON' line instead of the labeled 'Date:' transaction-date line; alternatively, applying batch locale inference to override an unambiguous label-bound date.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 034.jpg amount_correct=true but date_correct=false. The image is a Perniagaan Zheng Hui simplified tax invoice whose summary row shows 'Date: 09/03/2018' alongside a 'Time: 08:49:00' label and total 332.30; the written date '2018-08-09' is exactly the ISO form obtained by swapping day and month of '09/03/2018' only if misparsed, OR by picking a different date-shaped token elsewhere in the receipt. Either path indicates the date was not bound to the labeled transaction-date line under the declared DD/MM/YYYY locale.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Scan canonicalized lines for a 'DATE' / 'INVOICE DATE' label (allowing OCR variants DATA/DAIE), reject lines preceded by PRINT/CLOSED/CLOSING/FRN/LOYALTY/PROMO, parse the adjacent token under the declared Malaysian DD/MM/YYYY locale, and emit ISO 8601. Only use batch locale inference for genuinely ambiguous rows where both components are <=12.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale with the declared DD/MM/YYYY primary; fall through to receipt_date_lenient_parse only if the strict regex on the label-bound line fails.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to receipt-style OCR tasks that supply a locale or whose batch is dominated by one locale; limited to label-bound date extraction.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Free-form document date extraction, ambiguous locales where no label exists, or non-receipt timestamp parsing.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale

diagnoses.label: iteration_budget_exhausted_via_per_image_debug_loop
diagnoses.general_pattern: Running an interactive per-image debug loop (OCR → inspect → tweak heuristic → rerun) across a 22-image batch consumes the agent-iteration budget without converging the heuristics, resulting in termination at max_iterations rather than natural completion.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating each receipt as its own debug session with repeated terminal/think/file_editor cycles instead of running one diagnostic sweep that dumps per-variant OCR slices and candidate tuples for all images, then planning a small consolidated set of pattern/variant edits and re-running once.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Execution metadata reports agent_iterations=65, max_iterations_at_source=65, termination_reason='max_iterations', acp_stop_reason='max_turn_requests', with response_tool_call_counts {terminal:27, think:22, file_editor:16} and n_skill_invocations=0 (the loaded receipt overlay was never explicitly invoked). The partial trajectory ends with incremental tweaks to ocr_variants() (adding a 3x upscale + PSM 4 pass) rather than a batch replan.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: After the first full pass over all receipts, aggregate per-image candidate tuples and error modes, group failures by anchor (tier-priority mismatch, confusable, split-line, label-bound date), apply one consolidated edit per anchor family, then run once more; stop debugging individual images once the budget halves.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Follow the overlay's 'Workflow note: batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit': single diagnostic dump, consolidated edits grouped by mechanism anchor, single re-run.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to batch OCR extraction over N images where per-image interactive debugging would exceed the iteration budget.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Single-image tasks, non-OCR workflows, or tasks where per-item verification is explicitly required.
